observations: Forced ride: steer/jump/dash only, no backtracking, so crate placement is lane choice plus jump timing and every miss is permanent.
Groups of 1-5 crates about one per screen, separated by hazard beats; per-section counts 12/15/17/7.
S1 alternates crate lanes L-R-L before the first two-sided hazard asks for the same tempo.

Three towers, one prop (worker-held springboard), three answers: ignore / bounce / jump over; crates sit in the tunnel / on the roof / under the tower; loose lives on the wrong-answer roofs are decoys.
Two of three life crates float above the road - the count traps of the stage.
Every checkpoint is embedded in a crate group (W-C-W, slalom head, W+C).
Time crates total 29 s against a 16.9 s record: in time trial the crates are the race.
Pura crouches before jumps and on landing: time crates on stack tops need a landing timed just before the stack (TT fr.10).
Dash dissolves hazards (barrels, low dragons, crevices) but not the steering demand of the crate lines.
